I’ve been farming these 5 mu for 20 years, and I know every patch of soil. My household has five mouths to feed, and with some family working off-farm, I can’t be everywhere at once, so I have to be practical. I have well irrigation, which means I’m not completely at the mercy of the rain, but pumping costs money and labor, so I don’t waste water.

This year, I’ll keep my main **wheat-maize rotation on 2.5 mu** — it’s the safest bet for steady grain and income. I’ll put **1.5 mu into cotton** because the price has been decent lately and I know how to manage it, but it’s labor-heavy, so I can’t do more with the off-farm jobs in the family. I’ll plant **1 mu of peanut** on the sandier corner of my field; peanuts don’t need as much nitrogen because they fix their own, and the soil there suits them.

For **winter wheat**, I’ll sow an improved variety in mid-October. I’ll apply about 16 kg nitrogen, 7 kg phosphorus, and 5 kg potassium per mu. I’ll irrigate four times — at regreening, jointing, heading, and grain filling — because wheat needs steady moisture to set a good grain. I’ll spray pesticides twice for aphids and diseases. I use rotary tillage before sowing to get a fine seedbed. I expect around 500 kg per mu if the spring doesn’t turn too dry.

For **summer maize** on that same 2.5 mu, I’ll plant a hybrid right after wheat harvest in early June. I’ll put down 15 kg nitrogen, 6 kg phosphorus, and 5 kg potassium per mu. I’ll irrigate three times, especially at the big喇叭口 stage and flowering. Two pesticide sprays should handle armyworms and rust. I’ll do minimal tillage — just clear the stubble and plant quickly because the summer season is short. I expect about 550 kg per mu.

For **cotton** on 1.5 mu, I’ll plant a hybrid in late April. Cotton is hungry for potassium, so I’ll apply 14 kg nitrogen, 5 kg phosphorus, and 9 kg potassium per mu. I’ll irrigate three times at budding, flowering, and boll opening. Cotton pests are relentless — bollworms, aphids, mites — so I’ll spray five times. I’ll plough that patch deeply because cotton roots need loose soil. I expect about 280 kg of seed cotton per mu.

For **peanut** on 1 mu, I’ll sow an improved variety in early May. Peanuts don’t need much nitrogen, so I’ll apply only 7 kg, but 6 kg phosphorus and 9 kg potassium per mu for pod development. I’ll irrigate twice, at flowering and pod-setting. I’ll spray three times for leaf spot and aphids. Rotary tillage is enough. I expect about 300 kg per mu of pods.
